Hi Rishi,

Quick note from OptimaFinance — we're ramping faster than expected in EMEA and have a timing gap on our VC funding that will delay our usual 30-day remits for two upcoming invoices (Aug & Sep). To avoid impacting our production access we'd like to request a temporary Net60 for the next two invoices and a short-term credit cap while we close the round.

High-level ask:
- Temporarily move next two invoices to Net60
- Establish a short-term credit cap of $250,000 (rolling)
- Clarify how VAT will be handled for our EU subsidiary (we can provide VAT certs)

We can provide an interim payment guarantee and are open to a partial security deposit if that helps. Please let me know what documentation you need and any conditions Redwood would require. We value the service and want to keep usage uninterrupted.

Thanks,
Ana Lopez
VP Finance, OptimaHealth
ana.lopez@optimahealth.com

Hi Ana — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the ramp. We can absolutely try to build a short-term arrangement to keep you running while funding closes. High-level proposal from our side: 

1) Interim structure (60-day pilot, 2 invoices)
   - Security deposit equal to 20% of the first invoice due prior to issuance; deposits apply to invoices on receipt.
   - Redwood grants a rolling credit cap of $150,000 for 90 days while we monitor usage and remittance cadence.

2) Payment cadence suggestions
   - First invoice: Net30 but covered by the security deposit (reduces risk);
   - Second invoice: Net60 as requested;

3) Required documentation
   - VAT certificate for EU entity (we can accept your attachment)
   - Completed credit application (I attached a draft payment schedule to illustrate the cadence)

4) Timeline and next steps
   - If you can send the VAT cert and sign the payment schedule by EOD Thursday we'll route to finance for a quick credit review. Marissa — can you confirm whether the 20% deposit + rolling 150k is an approvable finance posture for Optima?

I attached: draft-payment-schedule.xlsx (staged invoices + deposit rows)
